After the Civil War young families from the old Pennsylvania farm counties went west by the thousand.
Adams County’s farms had been divided for generations; land in Illinois and Iowa was cheap,
and the railroads that had just crossed the prairie sold it on easy terms and advertised it back East.
Edward Wintrode, home from the war, spent the 1870s at Curwensville, in the lumber country of Clearfield County.
Then the family moved in step with Anna’s sister Rachel and her husband, John Maritz.
The Maritzes went to Lee County, Illinois, in 1875; the Wintrodes joined them in 1878,
and Harry was born there in 1880. That year the Wintrodes went on to Hayes Township in Ida County,
Iowa, eight miles south-east of Ida Grove, then still thinly settled, and the Maritzes followed them in 1884.
Edward and Anna farmed there for twenty-five years and are buried at Ida Grove.
